title: GOD REMEMBERS, AND SO SHOULD WE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'But for their sake I will remember the covenant with their ancestors
whom I brought out of Egypt in the sight of the nations to be their God.
I am the LORD.' These are the decrees, the laws and the regulations that
the LORD established at Mount Sinai between himself and the Israelites
through Moses" - Lev 26:45-46 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes as it is meant to — not on judgment, but on God's
remembering. For their sake, He says, I will remember the covenant. And
then a final signature: I am the LORD.

Look back over the whole chapter now. It began with blessings, moved
through solemn warnings, descended into exile and ruin, and then turned —
through confession and God's covenant faithfulness — back to mercy. The
last word is not wrath. The last word is God remembering His promise for
His people's sake.

Dear reader, this is the shape of the entire Bible in miniature. Human
faithfulness fails. Consequences come. But God's covenant love reaches
down, remembers, and restores. The story never ends on judgment for those
who turn to Him. It ends on grace.

And notice the phrase "for their sake." God's remembering was aimed at
their good. He was not merely keeping a legal agreement; He was acting out
of love for His people.

The covenant given at Sinai pointed forward to a better covenant, sealed
not in the blood of animals but in the blood of Christ (Heb 8:6). At the
Last Supper Jesus lifted the cup and said, this is the new covenant in my
blood (Luke 22:20). What God remembered for Israel's sake, He has
guaranteed for us in His Son.

Whatever this chapter has stirred in you — hold on to how it ends. God
remembers. Grace has the last word.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does the story of my life feel like it is ending on judgment or grace?
2. How does it comfort me that God's last word is mercy, not wrath?
3. What does the new covenant in Christ's blood mean for me personally?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that grace has the last word. You remember Your covenant
for Your people's sake, and You have sealed a new covenant in the blood of
Christ. I rest in Your faithful love. Amen.
